summary.headline: Somany Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 25% to INR854 crore with EBITDA margin at 11.7%; FY27 margin uplift guided up to 2-2.5%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR854 crore, up roughly 25%, with volume growth of about 5.5% and EBITDA margin of 11.7%, attributed to better plant utilisation, full pass-through of price increases and a richer product mix. Bathware grew about 18% (INR88 crore, 15% per the tiles-breakup remark) and Building Solutions about 28% (INR45 crore). Gas cost rose to about INR70/SCM from INR45 in FY26 and INR43 in Q2, and management says it has been fully passed on. Several plants were down for upgradation in July and August, which management says cost volume growth of about 1.5 percentage points. JV swing improved to a Q2 profit of INR3 crore versus a loss of INR12 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR723 crore, up about 27%. GVT share about 45%, up from about 40-41% a year ago; project share rising about 2-3 points.

segments.name: Bathware (sanitaryware and faucets)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR88 crore, about 15% growth. Sanitaryware growing about 20%, guided to 20% for FY27 and next year. Margins said to be a couple of points above tiles; brass-driven faucet margins were weaker in Q1.

segments.name: Building Solutions (adhesives etc.)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR45 crore, about 28% growth. Adhesives growing 40-50%, with a new plant commissioned in the north last month and a south plant started last quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at high single digits; Bathware guided at about 20%.
FY27 EBITDA margin improvement over FY26 revised to about 2-2.5%, up from an earlier 1-1.5%.
Management expects FY28 revenue growth at high single digits, and an EBITDA margin of 11.5-12% or higher in the next year.
Q3 volume expected to be better than H1 and EBITDA similar to or above Q2 in absolute terms; Q4 volume expected to be significantly better.
Marketing spend held at 2.3-2.5% of sales for the full year, in absolute terms higher than last year.
Expansion of about 16-17 million sq m (mainly GVT) due for production around September of next year; about 4 million sq m of annualised capacity added this year through debottlenecking.
capex_capacity: Siravit (South JV) capex of about INR250 crore, funded 50:50 debt and equity; Somany share about INR60 crore. Capacity to be expanded to about 11-12 million sq m from the earlier announced 9 million sq m.
Sanitaryware JV stake to be raised to 76% from 51% by buying additional shares; funded from internal accruals.
Modernisation at Sudha (about INR15 crore) and Vintage (about INR8 crore); routine standalone capex of about INR70-80 crore a year.
Upgradation of a northern line in October 2026 to cut cost and add capacity. A large northern building-solutions plant started last month.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as decent and resilient in both retail and projects. Morbi exports fell about 31.2% in value and about 44-45% in volume in the first five months; full-year industry exports seen at INR12,000-13,000 crore versus INR18,750 crore in FY26.
Full pass-through of price increases: about 16-17% cumulative from April 2026. Project pricing about 1.5 percentage points below channel but volume is higher.
Management says Morbi capacity is likely to shrink or stay flat for 18-24 months, which benefits the organised sector. About 35% of Morbi is shut and about 10% more is expected to close over Diwali.
Retail realisation about INR76 per sq m versus INR80.5 last year; project realisation about INR70 versus INR76 retail (per management comments on the gap).

qa_highlights.question: Can prices be held if gas prices correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas fell INR2-3 from April; cumulative price increases of 16-17% since April are fully passed through. Management holds gas at about INR70-71 near term, and expects it to settle at INR60-70 if the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only about 5% when peers reached double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 7-8% volume growth next quarter. Q2 was hit by about 20 days of downtime in July and some August downtime. Without it, volume would have been about 1.5 points higher.

qa_highlights.question: GVT mix and margin effect of new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: GVT at 45% (up from about 40-41%) and expected to reach 65-70% in 2-3 years, since all new capacity is GVT. GVT adds only a slight margin premium; overall margin guidance is 2-2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans, including Nepal JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No Nepal update was given. Capex covers the Siravit South JV expansion (INR250 crore total, about INR60 crore Somany share), the sanitaryware JV stake increase to 76%, Sudha and Vintage modernisation, and routine capex, all funded internally or through the 50:50 Siravit mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation and gas prices threaten production?
qa_highlights.answer: All running plants operated at full capacity apart from scheduled upgrades. Management said tiles stay cheaper than alternatives even if prices rise 50%, and that gas supply is adequate with price the only issue.

qa_highlights.question: Bathware margins and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware margins are a couple of points above tiles and most gas-driven price increases have been passed on. Faucets have only partly passed on brass costs, which roughly doubled in 1.5 years; Q1 was weaker and Q2 slightly better.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility linked to the Middle East war and freight costs; Morbi export recovery depends on freight rates and European demand, with December seasonally weak.
Brass cost inflation in faucets, where pass-through is incomplete.
Execution on the 16-17 million sq m GVT expansion and the Siravit capex, due around September next year.
Q3 volume and EBITDA recovery, which depends on no further plant downtime and on October trends holding.
Reliance on the Jaquar price lead in sanitaryware, which limits Bathware pricing.
Management declined to give FY28 absolute revenue guidance, citing oil and gas uncertainty.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing power and capacity additions, and raised the margin guidance. Cautious on gas and freight volatility and on export recovery, and declined to give absolute FY28 revenue numbers.
key_quotes: The EBITDA, due to better utilization, optimum utilization of machinery of our own plants and JVs, we have improved our EBITDA, and that stands at 11.7%.
As far as our working capital is concerned, we are in a fairly healthy position. Our receivable days are also probably the best in the industry.
The next 16 million -odd square meters which we are putting into production in the next 12 months, all of that is GVT, which means that GVT will become significantly higher.
Sanitaryware, we have grown at 20%, and we will grow at 20% for the entire year, and we are looking at a 20% again for the next year.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at high single digits (~8%) against a 25% Q2 print, with Bathware at ~20% and FY27 EBITDA margin up 2-2.5pp; backing is partial, mainly 16-17 mn sq m GVT capacity due around September next year (4 quarters out), ~4 mn sq m debottlenecking already added, plus full price pass-through of 16-17% cumulative since April 2026.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27 full year; FY28 next year
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided up 2-2.5pp over FY26 (raised from 1-1.5pp), Q2 margin at 11.7%, FY28 guided at 11.5-12% or higher, with full pass-through of 16-17% price increases and gas at about INR70/SCM.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 16-17 million sq m mainly GVT expansion is under construction for production around September of next year, plus about 4 million sq m debottlenecking already added this year and a north adhesives plant commissioned last month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew about 5.5% with about 1.5pp lost to downtime; management expects 7-8% next quarter and significantly better Q4, with FY27 tile volume of 79-80 million sq m.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already set out (Siravit INR250 crore, sanitaryware JV stake to 76%, Sudha and Vintage modernisation, routine INR70-80 crore a year) and plants ran at 100% capacity, so further announcements are plausible but the big expansion is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance was already raised to 2-2.5pp and Q3 EBITDA is guided at or above Q2, but FY27 revenue guidance was held at high single digits despite a 25% Q2 print, and gas and freight risks cap further raises.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas price volatility tied to the Middle East war, incomplete brass pass-through in faucets, and export recovery weakness (Morbi exports down about 31% in value) could pressure the guide, though management is confident on pricing.

rows.label: Morbi capacity shrink benefits organised sector
rows.why: About 35% of Morbi is shut with about 10% more expected to close over Diwali, and management expects no substantial capacity increase for 18-24 months.

rows.label: Sanitaryware JV stake raised to 76% from 51%
rows.why: Stake purchase to be funded from internal accruals and is already announced.

rows.label: Adhesives growth 40-50% with new plants
rows.why: Adhesives growing 40-50% with a north plant commissioned last month and a south plant started last quarter, supporting Building Solutions growth of about 28%.

tone.note: Management was confident on pricing pass-through, demand and capacity additions and raised FY27 margin guidance, but cautious on gas and freight volatility, export recovery and declined to give absolute FY28 revenue; analysts probed the volume gap versus peers and the GVT mix and margin effect.
